practiceQuestions.stem: A patient reports reproducible calf discomfort with walking. Resting ABI is normal, but clinical suspicion for PAD remains. Which next test may help establish exertional hemodynamic limitation?

options.text: Repeat only anatomic CTA
Exercise treadmill ABI
Immediate invasive angiography
Venography

practiceQuestions.rationale: Exercise ABI can help when exertional symptoms suggest PAD despite normal/borderline resting ABI; choose tests to answer the question rather than proceed directly to invasive imaging. [2024 multisociety PAD guideline].

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with lifestyle-limiting claudication has not tried structured exercise or guideline-directed risk reduction. Which approach is most consistent with contemporary guidance?

options.text: Revascularize because imaging shows stenosis
Offer supervised exercise and risk-factor therapy, then revisit goals and options
Use infrapopliteal intervention first
Intervene solely to prevent progression

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2025 SVS guideline places supervised exercise as first-line for intermittent claudication and cautions against intervention based only on imaging/hemodynamic metrics. Individual decisions remain clinical. [SVS 2025].

practiceQuestions.stem: A person has a cool, painful foot with newly absent pulses and sensory change over hours. What is the best general response?

options.text: Schedule elective outpatient ABI
Urgently involve a vascular-capable emergency team and assess limb viability
Start exercise and observe for a month
Wait for CTA before alerting vascular specialists

practiceQuestions.rationale: Acute limb ischemia is time critical; urgent specialist assessment and limb viability evaluation take priority. Imaging must not create avoidable delay. [ALI review].

practiceQuestions.stem: An ABI is unexpectedly high/noncompressible in a person with diabetes and CKD. Which principle is sound?

options.text: High ABI excludes PAD
Consider toe-based pressure/TBI and clinical context
Use ABI ratio as a stenosis percentage
Proceed directly to catheter therapy

practiceQuestions.rationale: Medial arterial calcification may make ankle arteries poorly compressible, so toe pressures/TBI and other physiological assessments may be informative. Do not treat one value as a diagnosis or indication. [2024 guideline].

practiceQuestions.stem: Which credential most directly signals a physician passed an examination focused on vascular ultrasound interpretation?

options.text: ABIM cardiovascular disease certification
RPVI via the PVI examination
ABVM Endovascular
ACGME accreditation

practiceQuestions.rationale: Inteleos/APCA describes RPVI as a physician vascular-imaging interpretation credential based on the PVI exam; it is distinct from clinical specialty training. [RPVI].

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description correctly distinguishes ABVM certification exams?

options.text: One ABVM exam automatically certifies vascular surgery

ABVM replaces medical licensure

practiceQuestions.rationale: Inteleos/APCA explicitly describes separate Vascular and Endovascular exam choices and requires physician applicants; it is a credential, not licensure or programme accreditation. [ABVM].

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official MGH listing says completed cardiovascular disease fellowship or equivalent and advises contacting the programme for specific application requirements. It does not state a case-volume threshold. [MGH].

practiceQuestions.stem: A noncompressible ABI conflicts with ulcers and ischemic symptoms. What should the learner do in an educational interpretation?

options.text: Report PAD absent because ABI is high
Integrate symptoms/exam with alternative perfusion tests and imaging as indicated
Assume CLTI staging solely from one test
Make revascularization decision from ABI alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABI can be noncompressible; clinical assessment and appropriate alternative physiological/imaging tests are used to answer the diagnostic question. A single test does not independently establish an intervention plan. [2024 guideline].

practiceQuestions.stem: A suspected lower-extremity DVT case has low clinical pretest probability. Which general diagnostic principle should guide testing?

options.text: Order serial angiography for all patients
Use a validated probability-based diagnostic pathway rather than ultrasound in isolation
Treat a negative test as proof of every venous diagnosis
Use arterial ABI as the confirmatory test

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASH guidelines use diagnostic strategies informed by clinical pretest probability and test characteristics; choose a validated pathway and follow it rather than interpreting imaging in isolation. [ASH VTE guideline].

practiceQuestions.stem: A proposed catheter intervention is supported only by an incidental stenosis on imaging in an asymptomatic person. What is the best evidence-aware answer?

options.text: Proceed because stenosis predicts limb loss
Do not infer an indication from imaging alone; clarify symptoms, risk, benefit and patient goals
Use the largest available device
Claim the intervention prevents progression

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2025 SVS claudication guideline recommends against revascularization solely on imaging or hemodynamic measurements in asymptomatic PAD; assess actual clinical presentation and evidence. [SVS 2025].

title: Breast Pathology Fellowship
prerequisites: Completed AP or AP/CP physician residency-level pathology; this self-study presumes competence in histology, tissue processing, IHC, and surgical pathology reporting.
Working familiarity with breast anatomy, cancer staging terminology, and basic statistics.
No course completion implies eligibility for MGB appointment, independent sign-out, licensure, or board certification.
objectives: Classify common benign, atypical, in-situ, invasive, fibroepithelial, papillary, stromal, and selected rare breast lesions using morphology-first reasoning.
Interpret ER/PR and HER2 biomarkers using current guideline versions and quality controls.
Produce structured biopsy and resection reports from available evidence while avoiding invented data.
Integrate radiology-pathology concordance, sampling limits, and multidisciplinary communication.
Recognize when consultation, additional sampling, or current guideline review is required.

topicGaps: Only three added recordings had both accessible public playback and an observed duration: 9,068 seconds (2.5194 hours). The 36-hour target therefore retains a 33.4811-hour residual gap.

All 13 inherited YouTube items remain uncounted because public runtime/playback and free access could not be established with allowed metadata checks; the visible playlist listing is not duration evidence.

Units 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11 and 12 have no new verified-duration lecture dedicated to their full scope. Existing entries mapped to those units remain unknown-duration, so coverage is not verified by runtime.

New free lectures are concentrated in post-neoadjuvant assessment, diagnostic pitfalls and IHC; no qualifying free-duration course was verified for normal handling, full benign spectrum, papillary/nipple lesions, special-type carcinomas, complete staging/margins, or rare inflammatory/vascular/hematolymphoid lesions.
CAP current protocols and teaching files support report/interpretation exercises but are readings or slides, not recordings and do not count toward the video floor.

Five newly authored episodes are complete scripts only. They are not rendered or counted. The source-based unit production plan allocates 33.4811 future hours; feasibility depends on further authored and recorded materials and is not demonstrated by target minutes.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The official institutional program identified is MGB’s collaborative Breast Pathology Fellowship at Brigham and Women’s Hospital and Massachusetts General Hospital. The programme page classifies it as non-GME; it is a clinical physician subspecialty fellowship, not a generic directory category or research-only/non-physician supplement. This course does not represent its private curriculum.

practiceQuestions.stem: A core biopsy shows monotonous low-grade cribriform proliferation spanning a measured 1.5 mm, with calcifications. What is the most defensible distinction to resolve before calling DCIS?

options.text: Whether the lesion exceeds quantitative threshold distinguishing ADH from low-grade DCIS
Whether HER2 is amplified
Whether a sentinel node is positive
Whether the patient has a family history

practiceQuestions.rationale: ADH versus low-grade DCIS depends on architectural/cytologic features and extent, with sampling context; biomarkers/nodes/family history do not determine that morphologic distinction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A papillary core shows fibrovascular cores and intact myoepithelial cells in cores and at the periphery. What is the best interpretive principle?

options.text: Use myoepithelial stains as a contextual adjunct with morphology and sampling
Diagnose carcinoma because any papillary lesion is malignant
Exclude papillary neoplasm because a core is limited
Use E-cadherin alone to classify all papillary lesions

practiceQuestions.rationale: Myoepithelial immunostains can support interpretation but have pitfalls and do not replace morphology or radiologic-pathologic context.

practiceQuestions.stem: An excision includes an invasive carcinoma and an in situ component. Which report approach is appropriate?

options.text: Use the current CAP invasive resection protocol and report required elements from available data
Infer pTNM from biopsy size and imaging alone
Report only histologic type
Omit margins because they are clinical data

practiceQuestions.rationale: The current CAP protocol specifies structured required elements; missing information should not be invented.

practiceQuestions.stem: An invasive breast carcinoma has ER staining in 90% of tumor nuclei with adequate controls. What is the correct core interpretation?

options.text: ER positive, with assay interpretation per current ASCO/CAP criteria
HER2 positive
ER negative due to incomplete staining
Cannot interpret without Ki-67

practiceQuestions.rationale: ER results are interpreted by current validated criteria and controls; HER2/Ki-67 do not override the ER result.

practiceQuestions.stem: A HER2 IHC result is equivocal by current scoring. What is the next principle?

options.text: Perform/interpret reflex in-situ hybridization per current guideline algorithm
Call positive based on low-level expression
Repeat ER only
Infer amplification from grade

practiceQuestions.rationale: Equivocal HER2 IHC requires guideline-directed reflex testing and appropriate integration; do not infer from grade.

practiceQuestions.stem: A cellular fibroepithelial lesion has stromal overgrowth, marked stromal atypia, and brisk mitoses. What is the key differential?

options.text: Malignant phyllodes tumor versus other spindle-cell lesions
Usual ductal hyperplasia versus ADH
DCIS versus LCIS
Papilloma versus Paget disease

practiceQuestions.rationale: Phyllodes grading integrates stromal cellularity, atypia, mitotic activity, overgrowth, and borders; the full specimen context is needed.

practiceQuestions.stem: A post-neoadjuvant resection shows a treated tumor bed and small residual invasive foci. Which reporting principle is sound?

options.text: Map the tumor bed and report residual disease using current protocol; do not equate fibrosis with complete response
Call pathologic complete response because treatment effect is present
Use pretreatment imaging size as residual tumor size
Ignore nodal response

practiceQuestions.rationale: Post-treatment assessment requires careful mapping and separate evaluation of residual invasive disease, DCIS, and nodes.

practiceQuestions.stem: A breast core diagnosis does not explain a highly suspicious imaging target. What is the appropriate action?

options.text: Flag radiologic-pathologic discordance for multidisciplinary reconciliation
Assume the benign core is definitive
Upgrade automatically to carcinoma
Repeat immunostains until concordant

practiceQuestions.rationale: Discordance is a quality/safety issue requiring communication and appropriate further evaluation, not automatic histologic upgrading.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about the MGB Breast Pathology Fellowship is supported by its official page?

options.text: It is a one-year BWH/MGH program with rotations at both sites and 39 clinical service weeks
It is an ACGME-accredited breast pathology subspecialty
It provides a separate ABPath breast board exam
Its online public didactics are all open-access

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official page documents one year, joint BWH/MGH rotations, and 39 service weeks; neither ACGME nor ABPath lists breast as a separate subspecialty board.

practiceQuestions.stem: A well-circumscribed breast mass has stromal leaf-like architecture and increased stromal cellularity. Which reasoning approach is best?

options.text: Assess the entire fibroepithelial lesion, including borders, atypia, mitoses, overgrowth, and sampling
Classify as fibroadenoma based on circumscription alone
Call phyllodes malignant based only on size
Order HER2 testing to distinguish fibroadenoma from phyllodes

practiceQuestions.rationale: Distinguishing fibroadenoma from phyllodes, and grading the latter, requires integrated stromal features and adequate sampling.
